**Finding submitted: deviation (medium, confidence 0.62)**

**What I checked**
- Read the full agreement (all four substantive sections) rather than relying on the planner's "likely absent" hint.
- **Section 3.1 (p0019)** — fees are 30% of Net Sales *above* $11,000/month: purely usage-based, no minimum spend, no volume cap. Compliant on its face.
- **Section 6.1 (p0037)** — a restriction on us, but exclusivity/field-of-use, not a volume or purchase commitment; out of scope for this rule.
- **Sections 1.2, 1.6, 1.8** — HDI bears all development, hosting and promotion costs; commitments running *to* us, not flagged.

**The issue — Section 4.2(a) (p0026)**
The term auto-renews annually (§4.1), and our only exit (90 days' notice) triggers a "Termination Payment" of half of our own trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000, payable in eight quarterly installments for services we will never receive. That is a take-or-pay-flavoured penalty on exit rather than a true-up — the precise economics the rule guards against ("we do not take-or-pay without an exit"; "replace shortfall penalties with a true-up").

**Redline (validated ok:true) — fallback level**
Given HDI genuinely funds the build and hosting, deletion would be disproportionate, so I made two minimal insertions into §4.2(a):
1. No Termination Payment where we terminate for HDI's breach or failure to launch under §1.6; and
2. The payment is capped at HDI's documented Site costs not already recovered through our §3 payments — converting the penalty into a cost true-up.

Note for the deal team: an adjacent termination-fee rule may also want to look at §4.2(c)'s eight-quarter installment tail.
